ai.description: This turtle reaches 100 cm in carapace length. It features a smooth, leathery, olive-brown shell and a small, pig-like snout. The head is broad with eyes positioned close to the tip of the snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pelochelys cantorii* is best distinguished by its extremely reduced, flat head and tiny, pig-like snout positioned at the very tip of its face, unlike other softshells.
ai.habitat: *Pelochelys cantorii* inhabits slow-moving, deep freshwater rivers and estuaries in low-lying tropical regions, often favoring areas with sandy banks and riparian vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle spends up to 95% of its life buried in riverbeds, emerging only briefly to ambush passing prey with a lightning-fast strike.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pelochelys cantorii* is oviparous, laying 20–50 spherical eggs in nests along riverbanks. In India, nesting typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle inhabits low-elevation riverine systems across Northeast India, primarily in the Brahmaputra and Ganges basins.
